title: People in Successful Projects: Leadership, Change and Communication

header.html: 2.1 Assess an approach to leadership and management of teams; 2.2 assess an approach to leading change and to the people affected by the project; 2.3 apply communications and the people central to the method; 2.4 apply the communication management approach and the change management approach
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: Leading change and the people affected
People central to the method and the Additional Information

html:
1Leading and managing teams

People are an element of the method in their own right: projects succeed or fail through people, and every exam scenario has people in it.

Leadership inspires and guides people toward a goal. Management plans, organizes and controls the work within limits. A project manager needs both. The exam asks whether the approach fits these people in this situation.

Team leadership Effective Not fit for purpose
Style Adapts to the person: more direction for a newcomer, more freedom for an expert One style for all; micromanages experts; abandons newcomers
Roles and goals Clear roles, shared objectives, known authority Unclear roles; nobody sure who decides
Capability and competence Gaps found early and closed by training, pairing or extra skills Work assigned regardless of skill; gaps found at delivery
Diversity Different views invited and used One voice dominates
Trust Problems raised early without blame Bad news hidden; blame culture
Several parties Agreed ways of working across customer, supplier and remote teams Assumes everyone shares the same habits
Exam tip

. Capability is what the team can do; competence is what one person can do. A named person lacking a skill is a competence issue; a team lacking capacity or tools is a capability issue.

2Leading change and the people affected

Change management helps people move from the current way of working to the new one so that the benefits are realized. A project can deliver on time and still fail if nobody adopts the result. Two groups matter: people within the project (the project management team) and people affected by the project (users, operations staff, customers). A stakeholder can be either.

The change management approach, a PID product, says who is affected and how, how they will be involved, trained and supported, and how adoption will be measured.

Change Effective Not fit for purpose
Impact Analyzes early who is affected and how (berth agents lose paper permits) Assumes people will adapt after delivery
Involvement Affected people help design and test the service The change arrives as a surprise
Readiness and support Training and time to adjust planned before go-live Training cut to save time or money
Resistance Concerns listened to and causes addressed Resistance ignored or punished
Ownership Senior user and executive visibly lead the change Left to the project team alone
Adoption Use measured and linked to the benefits Ends at delivery
Exam tip

. Delivering the product is not delivering the change. If the product is delivered but people do not use it, the gap is change management, led with the senior user.

3Communication and stakeholders

Communication is two-way, planned and fitted to the audience. The communication management approach, also a PID product, records who needs what information, when, through which channel, from whom, and how feedback is gathered. It rests on stakeholder analysis: identify stakeholders, analyze interest and influence, plan engagement, engage and review. The project manager owns it, and board members help by engaging the groups they speak for.

Communication Effective Not fit for purpose
Stakeholder analysis Everyone within and affected is found, analyzed and kept up to date Only the board is listed; analysis done once
Engagement Matched to each group: high influence and interest means close involvement The same message for everyone
Channel and frequency Fits the audience: a short note for a busy executive, a briefing for harbor staff A long report to all; a channel nobody reads
Feedback Two-way; gathered, answered and acted on One-way broadcast
Timing Bad news and needed decisions travel at once Held back for the next scheduled report
The approach Reviewed and changed as stakeholders change Written once and filed

Tailoring. A small co-located team may rely on daily conversation and a one-page approach. A large multi-party project needs formal channels and a written plan. Agile teams use daily meetings and visible boards, but stakeholders still need engaging.

Exam tip

. A one-size report is a red flag. If every audience gets the same document at the same time with no way to reply, the approach is not fit for purpose.

4People central to the method and the Additional Information

The people central to the method are the project management team (board, project manager, team managers, assurance and support) and the key stakeholders around them. The Additional Information in the exam describes some of them: skills, attitudes, time and preferences. Use each fact to choose the action.

Fact about a person What it suggests
A very busy executive Short, decision-focused reports; delegate through the project manager and assurance
A senior user who doubts the new service Involve early, listen, show how concerns are met
A team manager new to the platform More guidance, closer checkpoints, pairing
A supplier lead who reads only brief updates A short written summary with the decision needed
Assurance staff who also work on the delivery An independence problem: assurance must be independent of the project manager
A team split across two organizations Agreed channels, regular check-ins, shared tools

Judge an approach in four steps: who the people are, what the situation is, what approach was used, and whether it fits these people. Then name the product that records it.

Exam tip

. If a question names a person, the Additional Information usually changes the best answer. Match the action to that person's skills, time, attitude or position.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1The Additional Information says Wei Chen's Delta Software developers are new to the permit platform. Sam Okafor gives them no guidance, saying strong teams need freedom. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because freedom works best for every team whatever its experience
  • BYes, because a supplier's team should never be directed by the customer
  • CNo, because the style should fit the team's experience and support needs
  • DNo, because the project manager should keep every decision with himself
Show the answer

Answer: C. Effective team leadership adapts to the people's capability and competence, and newcomers need more direction and support.

S2Project Harbor will change how berth agents request permits, yet Sam Okafor plans no contact or training for them until after rollout. What should Sam do?

  • AInvolve the berth agents now and plan their training and support
  • BWait until rollout ends and then email the agents their instructions
  • CLeave the agents to the senior supplier, who knows the new platform
  • DNote their likely reaction as a risk and review it after rollout
Show the answer

Answer: A. The change management approach should involve affected people early and plan training and support before go-live.

S3Sam wants to record which Project Harbor stakeholders need which information, when, through which channel and from whom. Which management product should hold this?

  • AThe change management approach
  • BThe communication management approach
  • CThe benefits management approach
  • DThe project product description
Show the answer

Answer: B. The communication management approach records who needs what information, when, how and from whom, plus the feedback route.

S4At the start of Project Harbor, Sam lists only the project board as stakeholders and never reviews the list. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because only the board has authority to make decisions in the project
  • BYes, because a fixed list avoids confusion about whom the project must inform
  • CNo, because affected people are stakeholders too and the list needs review
  • DNo, because the executive must compile the stakeholder list for the project
Show the answer

Answer: C. Stakeholder analysis covers everyone who can affect or is affected by the project and must be kept up to date.

S5The Additional Information says Lena Kovac, the senior supplier, travels often and reads only short written updates. Sam must tell her about a delay that needs her decision. What should Sam do?

  • ASend a short note with the delay, its impact and the decision needed
  • BHold the news until the next board meeting and explain it to her there
  • CSend the full stage plan so that she can find the delay herself
  • DAsk Wei Chen to mention the delay to her informally this week
Show the answer

Answer: A. The channel and style must fit the person, and a decision that is needed should travel at once rather than wait for a meeting.

S6Which management product records how Project Harbor will help berth agents and harbor staff adopt the online permit service?

  • AThe communication management approach
  • BThe benefits management approach
  • CThe change management approach
  • DThe project product description
Show the answer

Answer: C. The change management approach says who is affected, how they will be supported and how adoption will be measured.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the difference between leadership and management?

Show the answer

Leadership inspires and guides people; management plans and controls the work.

R2Which three qualities of an effective team does the method stress?

Show the answer

Diversity, capability and competence.

R3What is the change management approach for?

Show the answer

How the project helps affected people adopt the change.

R4What does the communication management approach record?

Show the answer

Who needs what information, when, how and from whom, and how feedback is gathered.

R5Define a stakeholder.

Show the answer

Anyone who can affect, is affected by, or believes they are affected by the project.

R6Which document holds both approaches?

Show the answer

The PID.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Leadership and management inspire people and guide them; plan and control the work; fit style to the person
Team qualities diversity, capability (team) and competence (person)
Change move people to the new way; involve early, train and support, measure adoption
Within and affected project management team; users, operations staff and customers
Communication two-way, planned, fitted to the audience, with feedback
Stakeholders identify, analyze interest and influence, plan, engage, review
Approaches change and communication management approaches, both parts of the PID
Additional Information facts about named people; use them to choose the action
